review.content: Trinity Adapter on THEM 909 — Surprisingly Good Upgrade I tried a Trinity adapter on my THEM 909 because I wanted to turn the boot into more of an urban/cruising setup without giving up the fit and feel of the 909. The biggest difference is versatility. The 909 is originally a UFS aggressive skate, so with the adapter I can use Trinity frames and experiment with bigger-wheel setups for cruising, longer distances, and city skating. The 909 shell itself is supportive enough that bigger wheels actually make sense on it. The setup feels more responsive and much faster compared with the normal aggressive configuration. Bigger wheels obviously roll over rough pavement much better, and the 909 gives enough lateral support that it doesn't feel completely out of place as an urban skate. There is one compromise: stack height. Because you're putting an adapter between a UFS boot and a Trinity frame, you don't get the full low-to-the-ground advantage that a native Trinity boot provides. There's also extra hardware and a little extra weight. So if your only goal is Trinity skating, a native Trinity boot is still the cleaner solution. But if you already own and love your THEM 909, this is a really interesting conversion. You basically get two personalities from one boot: UFS for aggressive skating and Trinity/big wheels for cruising and urban skating. Pros: more frame choices, bigger-wheel capability, much better cruising, keeps the familiar 909 boot and liner. Cons: added stack height, additional hardware/weight, and it's not as elegant as native Trinity mounting. Overall: 8/10. A very cool upgrade for 909 owners who want one boot that can do more than aggressive skating.

These are excellent inline skates, perfect even for people with wide feet. I had a hard time finding the right size, so here are some of my findings and measurements in case it may help someone. This is still subjective in some respects, so please take it with a grain of salt. - Don’t rely on your street shoe size; measure your longest foot in cm (Mondo size) and check Seba CJ2 Prime's official size chart on their website. - Different sizes share the same shell. EU size 39 corresponds to the same shell as size 40, and the same goes for sizes 41–42, 43–44, etc. If between two shell sizes, if the smallest fits, take this one. - Liner will expend half to a full EU size (you should be snug/tight at first). - Try on the boot barefoot without the liner, with your longest foot, no socks. Touch the inside front of the shell with your longest toe and measure the gap between your heel and the back of the shell: a gap of less than 1 finger indicates a very tight “pro” fit; 1 to 1.5 finger indicates a tight and precise fit but still comfortable after a few sessions ; between 1.5 and 2.5 is comfort fit from the get go but it might become loose after some time (heel lift, sliding foot) ; more than 2.5 is definitly too big in my opinion. - In my case, choosing the smaller shell wasn’t possible, even though my foot is 25.9 cm long (I wear EU 42 street shoes) and size 40 skates should have been perfect according to the Seba size chart. It was definitly too small. Because of the width of my foot (10.5 cm) and the shape of my forefoot (the “Greek” type), size 41 EU fits me very well (pretty tight at first, snug and comfortable after a few sessions).

Brilliant set of boots, love them. Great looking and great performance; stiff and responsive. Can effortlessly get up to high speed and maintain it! Really fun to skate in, especially on the Endless frames. Would recommend.
Comments on fit: - Agree with 'sizing guide' for fit. - Toe-box has plenty space widthwise. Super tight height-wise. Almost too tight, lost feeling in my toes the first few skates, whilst breaking them in. After break in and heat moulding, much better. - Locking in Heel/Heel fit: Perform heat moulding, at 100degC no issues and easy to do. Instruction video available on YouTube. Before heat moulding had difficulty getting my heel locked in. After heat moulding, no problems and makes the boot much more comfortable and fun to skate in. (Also recommend replacing laces with power slide waxed laces, makes it easier to tighten the laces properly and secure your heel [140cm length] laces are the mechanism in these boots for securing the heel, not the Boa knob!) - Cuff, stiff and supportive. Do heat moulding to get it to wrap in around your shin for better support.
Comments on build quality: - Quality of build you would expect for boots at this price point. Very high. -A little disappointed in the carbon fiber finish, small voids and seams visible. All minor cosmetic only and only an issue if you know what to look for. - Can't fault the build and finish of the uppers, great! Sewn seams well finished and all glued seams good and lasted thru heat moulding, no issue. Materials seem though and long lasting. - Microfiber lining, good for securing your foot. Bit annoying when putting the boot on, as they grip your socks whilst your foot slides in, so you really need to open the boot to put these boots on.
In summary: Great boot, great build quality but Heat moulding is a must to get the most from them, with the improved fit.
